# color-spaces.library: Lerp

**Status:** Supported (tier `graphics`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> Component-wise linear interpolation; t is unclamped. Interpolating in XYZ
> is a straight radiance blend — perceptually non-uniform, which is what
> ColorLab and OkLab exist for.

## Signature

```plato
Lerp(a: ColorXYZ, b: ColorXYZ, t: Number): ColorXYZ
```

### Law_LerpAtZeroIsStart2D

```plato
// Lerp endpoints, now derived from Add + Between rather than written per type.
Law_LerpAtZeroIsStart2D(a: Point2D, b: Point2D): Boolean
    => a.Lerp(b, 0.0).Distance(a) <= 1e-4;
```

### Line 81

**Source:** [stdlib/graphics/color-spaces.library.plato, line 81](../../../../../stdlib/graphics/color-spaces.library.plato#L81).

```plato

    // Component-wise linear interpolation; t is unclamped. Interpolating in XYZ
    // is a straight radiance blend — perceptually non-uniform, which is what
    // ColorLab and OkLab exist for.
    Lerp(a: ColorXYZ, b: ColorXYZ, t: Number): ColorXYZ
        => (a.X + (b.X - a.X) * t,
            a.Y + (b.Y - a.Y) * t,
            a.Z + (b.Z - a.Z) * t);
```
